\begin{theorem}[Children, parents, and transitivity]\label{thm:children_transitivity}\label{thm:nested-refinement}
Suppose that $\Qcal$ refines $\Pcal$ through $\rho$.  Then
\[
P_\alpha Q_\beta
=
Q_\beta P_\alpha
=
\begin{cases}
Q_\beta & \rho(\beta)=\alpha,\\
0 & \rho(\beta)\ne\alpha.
\end{cases}
\]
Hence $Q_\beta X\subseteq P_{\rho(\beta)}X$.  If a third packet system $\Rcal$ refines $\Qcal$, then $\Rcal$ refines $\Pcal$ through the composite parent map.
\end{theorem}
records.proof_scope_analysis: Refines contains precisely the printed onto parent and coarse sum over children. Both absorption directions are derived by distributing this sum and applying fine-family idempotence/annihilation. Image inclusion is the immediate pointwise consequence of left absorption, and trans constructs the composite onto parent and proves its reconstruction. No nonzero ambient space or scalar field restriction is added; semiring/module scope is stronger.
records.certificate_analysis: The assumed refinement relation is the hypothesis of the theorem, not a supplied absorption or transitivity conclusion.

\begin{theorem}[Common refinement of commuting packet systems]\label{thm:common_refinement}
Let $\Pcal=(P_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ and $\Qcal=(Q_\beta)_{\beta\in J}$ be packet systems on $X$.  Assume
\[
P_\alpha Q_\beta=Q_\beta P_\alpha
\]
for all $\alpha$ and $\beta$.  Remove the zero operators from the family
\[
R_{\alpha\beta}=P_\alpha Q_\beta.
\]
The remaining operators form a packet system that refines both $\Pcal$ and $\Qcal$.  The same statement holds for any finite collection of pairwise commuting packet systems.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Finite precision]\label{cor:finite-precision}
Let $F^\bullet R$ be a multiplicative decreasing filtration and let
$q_L:R\to R_L$ be a ring homomorphism that kills $F^L R$. Suppose
\[
H=\sum_{e\in E}H_e,
\qquad D^{-1}H_e\in F^{w(e)}R,
\qquad w(e)\ge1,
\]
with $E$ finite. Then $q_L(D^{-1}H)^L=0$, the finite sum in
\cref{thm:weighted-inverse}(a) is a two-sided inverse after applying $q_L$,
and its word expansion may discard every word of weight at least $L$.
More explicitly, for a length cutoff $N$, define
\[
S^{\mathrm{pr}}_{L,N}
=
\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}(-1)^n
\sum_{\substack{\gamma\in E^n\\W(\gamma)<L}}A_\gamma.
\]
Lean proves directly that $q_L(S^{\mathrm{pr}}_{L,N})$ equals the mapped
geometric inverse whenever $q_L(A^N)=0$, and hence is a two-sided inverse of
$q_L(I+A)$, where $A=\sum_eA_e=D^{-1}H$. With the supplied two-sided
inverse $D^{-1}$ of $D$, this gives the explicit two-sided inverse
\[
\boxed{q_L\!\left(S^{\mathrm{pr}}_{L,N}D^{-1}\right)}
\quad\text{of}\quad q_L(D+H).
\]
If every edge weight is at least $m$ and $L\le mN$, then the nilpotence
condition follows from the filtration data because
$m|\gamma|\le W(\gamma)$. For $m>0$, the executable choice
$N=\lceil L/m\rceil$ satisfies $L\le mN$. This elementary ceiling inequality
is also proved in Lean. The choice $m=1,N=L$ gives the standard cutoff.
In the DVR example $q_L:R\to R/\pi^L R$, this reads
\[
q_L(T)^{-1}
=
q_L\!\left(\sum_{W(\gamma)<L}
(-1)^{|\gamma|}A_\gamma D^{-1}\right).
\]
\end{corollary}
records.proof_scope_analysis: MultiplicativeFiltration supplies only additive closure, decreasing levels and multiplicative level addition. PrecisionCertificate means exactly q kills F^L. Ordered List products acquire summed weight by induction, the full power expands over all Fin n edge tuples, and high-weight terms vanish under q. Positive/minimum edge weights derive the nilpotence cutoff, rather than assuming it in the final positive-weight endpoint. Explicit signed pruned sum and right Dinv factor give both inverse equations; the elementary ceiling cutoff is proved.
records.certificate_analysis: PrecisionCertificate is the explicit q_L hypothesis, not the inverse conclusion. The intermediate pow_eq_zero theorem has an explicit nilpotence premise, but the final weighted-edge theorems construct that premise from the filtration and weight bounds.

\begin{theorem}[Automatic finite-graph transfer-zeta rationality]\label{thm:transfer-zeta}
Assume the vertex and edge sets are finite and every edge has positive integer
weight. For every $n$, exact enumeration of edge tuples of lengths at most
$n$, followed by endpoint and total-weight filtering, returns $a_n(s,t)$.
These coefficients obey the recurrence obtained by removing the first edge
\[
a_n(s,t)
=
\mathbf 1_{s=t,\,n=0}
+\sum_{\substack{e:\,\operatorname{source}(e)=s\\w(e)\le n}}
a_{n-w(e)}(\operatorname{target}(e),t).
\]
Let
\[
T(t)=I-A(t),\qquad
Q(t)=\det T(t),\qquad
P_{s,t}(t)=\operatorname{adj}(T(t))_{s,t}.
\]
Then $Q(0)=1$, hence $Q\ne0$ and $Q$ is a unit in $\Z[[t]]$, and the
independently enumerated walk series satisfies
\[
\boxed{
Z_{s,t}(t)=Q(t)^{-1}P_{s,t}(t),
\qquad
Q(t)Z_{s,t}(t)=P_{s,t}(t)
}
\quad\text{in }\Z[[t]].
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_scope_analysis: ExactWalk is the independent unrestricted ordered-list type with endpoint and weight constraints. Positive edge weights bound length; the bounded-tuple/list equivalence establishes exact finite enumeration including repeated/parallel edges. Actual first-edge bijections derive the recurrence and Z=I+AZ. Determinant and adjugate are computed from the finite adjacency matrix; Q(0)=1 is proved. A constructed inverse of Q and the two adjugate identities give a two-sided matrix inverse, and uniqueness identifies it with enumerated Z. Thus both printed entry identities are derived from graph data alone.
records.certificate_analysis: The additionally listed RationalCertificate.certificate_explicit_rationality DOES assume a coefficientwise rationality certificate and is not decisive evidence for this theorem. The certificate-free endpoints listed here close the statement and do not call that API.

\begin{corollary}[Linear recurrence]\label{cor:zeta-recurrence}
With the canonical polynomials from \cref{thm:transfer-zeta}, write
\[
Q(t)=\sum_kq_kt^k,
\qquad
Z_{s,t}(t)=\sum_{n\ge0}a_n(s,t)t^n.
\]
Then the walk counts satisfy the recurrence with constant coefficients determined by
$Q$ after the finite initial range contributed by $P_{s,t}$, with $\deg 0=-\infty$:
\[
\boxed{
\sum_{k=0}^{n}q_k a_{n-k}(s,t)=0
\qquad\bigl(n>\deg P_{s,t}\bigr).
}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluated B\'ezout spectral projector]\label{thm:bezout-projector}
Let $F,G,U,V\in\End_K(\Lambda\otimes_\OO K)$ and let $r\in K^\times$.
Suppose
\[
UF+VG=rI,
\qquad FG=0,
\qquad FG=GF,
\qquad GU=UG.
\]
Put $N=VG$. Then
\[
\boxed{N^2=rN.}
\]
Consequently the operator
\[
\boxed{
E=r^{-1}VG
}
\]
is idempotent, acts as the identity on $\ker F$, and acts as zero on
$\ker G$. If $V$ and $G$ preserve $\Lambda$, then
\[
rE=VG\in\End_\OO(\Lambda).
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_scope_analysis: Minimal unbundled theorems require exactly UF+VG=rI, FG=0, Commute F G, Commute G U and r nonzero where needed. They derive N(UF)=0, N^2=rN, E^2=E, actual kernel actions, and rE=VG. Lattice preservation uses only that V and G preserve the additive lattice; every O-lattice specializes to it.
records.certificate_analysis: The legacy EvaluatedBezoutCertificate carries six commutations and would be too restrictive as the sole witness for the printed minimal hypotheses. The decisive _of_bezout endpoints use only the two printed commutations and do not assume idempotence or kernel conclusions.

\begin{theorem}[Projector precision delay]\label{thm:precision-delay}
Let $E$ be a rational projector with $\pi^sE(\Lambda)\subseteq\Lambda$. If
\[
x\equiv y\pmod{\pi^{m+s}\Lambda},
\]
then
\[
Ex\equiv Ey\pmod{\pi^m\Lambda}.
\]
Thus $m+s$ input digits suffice to determine $m$ output digits of the projected packet.
\end{theorem}

Given the printed clearing property pi^s E preserves Lambda, the output witness is pi^s E z. Linearity and pow_add derive E x-E y=pi^m(pi^s E z). Idempotence is unnecessary, making the theorem stronger; no completeness or input-integrality restriction is added.

\begin{proposition}[Odd-adic versus dyadic behavior]\label{prop:dyadic-sign}
For every prime $p\ne2$, every entry of $E_+$ and $E_-$ is $p$-integral,
and each projector has exact local denominator weight zero. At $p=2$, each
projector has exact local denominator weight one. Multiplication by $2$ makes
it integral, while the unscaled matrix is not integral:
\[
s_{2,\Z_2^2}(E_+)=s_{2,\Z_2^2}(E_-)=1.
\]
The characteristic factors $x-1$ and $x+1$ have resultant $2$. Its $2$-adic
valuation is one, exactly the two local projector weights above, and its
$p$-adic valuation is zero at every prime $p\ne2$.
\end{proposition}

New operators are literal casts of those matrices acting on Padic p^2; standardLattice is coordinatewise PadicInt membership. Odd-prime inverse2 has norm1; at 2 the e_2 image has coordinate norm2>1, while 2E preserves the lattice. Least-exponent definition then gives exactly one.

\begin{theorem}[Concrete Smith-weighted congruence solve]\label{thm:smith-solve}
Let $p>1$ and consider the diagonal system over
$(\Z/(p^L)\Z)^d$
\[
\diag(p^{s_1},\ldots,p^{s_d})x=b
\pmod{p^L}.
\]
The system is solvable if and only if
\[
p^{\min(s_i,L)}\mid (b_i)_{\mathrm{val}}
\]
for every $i$, where $(b_i)_{\mathrm{val}}$ is the canonical natural
representative. Conditional on this admissibility condition, the number of
solutions is
\[
\boxed{
p^{\sum_{i=1}^d\min(s_i,L)}.
}
\]
If any coordinate is inadmissible, the solution set is empty and its
cardinality is zero.
\end{theorem}
records.proof_scope_analysis: The fibre is the actual additive multiplication-by-p^s fibre in ZMod(p^L). Solvability is proved by natural representatives and divisibility, with the two s<=L/L<=s cases. Inhabited fibres translate to the actual kernel; cyclic group kernel cardinality is gcd(p^L,p^s)=p^min(s,L). Concrete coordinate certificates are assembled from these independent arithmetic proofs, then a dependent product gives the full count and the zero branch. p>1 suffices even when composite. L=0 and empty dimension are valid.
records.certificate_analysis: Generic SmithCoordinateCertificate and SmithCardinalityCertificate do contain the target local facts, so generic product-count wrappers alone do not establish arithmetic. The decisive concrete ZMod constructors prove both fields, and the concrete global endpoints use those constructors. This historical label is diagonal ZMod scope only; general DVR rectangular scope belongs to the new Smith modules under other labels.

\begin{theorem}[Power defect identity]\label{thm:power_defect}\label{thm:power-defect}
For every integer $n\geq1$,
\[
CT_f^n-T_c^nC
=
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T_c^{n-1-k}\Delta T_f^k.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Norm bound]\label{cor:defect-norm}
For a submultiplicative operator norm,
\[
\|CT_f^n-T_c^nC\|
\le
\|\Delta\|
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}
\|T_c\|^{n-1-k}\|T_f\|^k.
\]
If $\|T_f\|,\|T_c\|\le\rho$, then
\[
\boxed{
\|CT_f^n-T_c^nC\|
\le n\rho^{n-1}\|\Delta\|.
}
\]
\end{corollary}
records.proof_scope_analysis: The first inequality is the actual typed operator-norm bound. The majorant uses the supplied bounds norm(Tf),norm(Tc)<=rho, derives rho>=0, bounds each summand by rho^(n-1), and counts n terms. It includes n=0 and zero fine/coarse spaces. Printed operator norms are the norms on the bounded operators of the preceding Banach-space context.
records.certificate_analysis: The only inequalities assumed are the printed norm(Tf),norm(Tc)<=rho; the defect and n-power estimate are proved.
